attested.notes: Voice pass against the over-humanising rule, plus the cluster timing reconciliation. Removed nine manufactured moments, most of them emotional rather than informative: the brown HMRC envelope and quiet dread in the opening, the Gazette notice imagined being seen by a neighbour or future employer, the hand-over feeling abrupt after years of carrying the thing, directors pulling records together at the kitchen table the night before, someone staring at a business account that will not cover wages, the debt that keeps a director awake, where a director's real fear sits, the quiet fear that asking questions puts you on HMRC's radar, and the fear of never using the trading name again. Each replaced with the useful thing it was dressing: who actually monitors Gazette notices, that creditors should be redirected to the liquidator from appointment day, that what matters before the first call is knowing which records are genuinely missing, that the largest debt is rarely the one causing difficulty afterwards, and that the first column of the risk table applies to every director regardless of conduct. The employees section used almost the exact phrasing flagged as borrowed empathy, so it now answers the practical question: whether to tell staff before or after appointment, agreed with the proposed liquidator. Timing reconciled with the timeline page: 6-12 and 12-24 months are now labelled the liquidator's active work rather than time to dissolution, with the statutory three months and the 712-day median added.
